newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rashid Hussain sees stocks recovering in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Rashid Hussain sees stocks recovering in 2nd half.

text.p: Rashid Hussain, executive chairman of RHB Capital Bhd RHBC.KL and Malaysia's biggest institutional broker, said on Monday the Malaysian stock market was expected to recover in the second half of the year.

The fall in stock prices over the last few months was a correction caused by fears of overexposure of banks to property sector and share financing and problems in Thailand, he told Reuters in an interview.
"That has been corrected and the dust has settled down. ...I am inclined to believe the second half is going to be better than the first half," he said.
He said the 10-15 percent correction in recent months was also due to speculation on "whether Malaysia is the next Thailand".

He said the recent speculative attack on the Thai baht and the subsequent flotation of the currency by Thailand has had its ramifications on Malaysia "at least in how foreign investors perceive their investments generally in the region".
"My own feeling is that Malaysia is not in the Thai boat. The economy still looks strong and minor adjustments are inevitable. Valuations do not look outrageous at all," he said.
"First half (corporate) earnings (are due). When they come in, they will add to the arguement (that) there is value in Malaysian stocks," Rashid said.
But the return of foreign investors, many of whom have downgraded Malaysia, would be gradual, he said.

The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks, peaked at 1,270.67 on February 28, just prior to the release of Bank Negara's 1996 annual report, which contained the new policy measures.
By May 16 the index had plummeted to 1,041.91.
